_about: fak position rows for the 'models' group. dim_id links each to a _taxonomy.json dimension.

rows.axis: Hardware / format coverage and portability of quantized kernels
rows.competitor: vLLM (FP8 on Hopper/Ada/Blackwell + MI300X via hipBLASLt/aiter); SGLang (FP8 MI300X); TensorRT-LLM (NVFP4 Blackwell); llama.cpp (broad CPU/GPU GGUF + FP4)
rows.comparison_note: Disclosed coverage gap where fak still TRAILS SOTA engines: fak now ships native SM120 NVFP4 W4A4 prefill, FP8/NVFP4/fp8k_nvfp4v KV cache, Q4_K MMQ (sm_80+), and native CUDA/Vulkan/Metal/CPU kernels for Q2_K..Q8_0 and IQ1_M..IQ4_NL (plus host AWQ/GPTQ). However, it lacks Hopper/Ada/MI300X FP8 W8A8 GEMMs, GPU AWQ/GPTQ device kernels, and production MXFP4 MoE coverage that vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, and llama.cpp accelerate across targets.

rows.axis: Hardware-shape neutrality: explicit fences for host-CPU assumptions
rows.competitor: vLLM plugin backends; llama.cpp backend matrix; MLC-LLM / TVM compilation
rows.unit: of 7 host-shape assumptions explicitly FENCED in the compute HAL contract
rows.fak_doc: docs/explainers/hardware-portability.md plus internal/compute/compute.go: Dtype/QuantSpec, Tensor/Host, Register/Pick/Tier, Caps.Async/Read/Argmax, whole-op Backend methods, Layout, WeightSource/Upload
rows.comparison_note: This corrects the GPU-bias in a pure backend-breadth row. fak still TRAILS the mature engines on how many accelerator families it serves, but it has a FENCED contract for the seven host-shape assumptions the HAL explainer names: (1) float32 monoculture -> Dtype/QuantSpec, (2) host-pointer aliasing -> Tensor/Host/Read boundary, (3) x86 build-tag dispatch -> runtime registry and Tier, (4) synchronous return-by-value -> Caps.Async with explicit Read/Argmax fences, (5) goroutine-only parallelism -> whole-op Backend methods, (6) row-major only -> Layout descriptor, and (7) eager full-RAM plus little-endian host -> WeightSource and Upload. Provenance labels: contract FENCED in code and docs; CUDA/Vulkan/Metal/CPU backends WITNESSED where their support rows say so; broad vendor conformance remains not-yet until the BCK/fak-certified work lands. apples_to_apples=false because this dimension measures contract shape, not device count or throughput.

rows.axis: Maximum parameter count & frontier-MoE architecture coverage
rows.competitor: llama.cpp (72B CPU / ~32B Metal; Qwen3-30B-A3B MoE @ 50 tok/s) · SGLang (multi-GPU TP, 27B+ quantized)
rows.competitor_source: HERO-BENCHMARK-2026-06-21.md ('Model-size ceiling on this box' fence); CLAIMS.md; llama.cpp model support (72B CPU / Qwen3-30B-A3B MoE)
rows.comparison_note: HW-WITNESSED on RTX 5080 16 GB (rtx5080-inkling2-v060/perf-receipt-v2.json): fak-native serves Inkling-2-Mini (26B hybrid MoE, UD-Q3_K_XL) on a single consumer NVIDIA GPU, and Qwen3.8-27B BF16 TP2 / Q4_K_M on datacenter/laptop CUDA (issue-8623, cuda-prefill-sm120), fronting SGLang/vLLM for frontier 100B-1T models. Historical M3 Pro Inkling-2-Mini vendored Splash receipts were retired and retracted as fak-native Metal claims (pure internal/metalgemm resident M3 Pro receipts pending). Trails llama.cpp (72B CPU) and SGLang multi-GPU TP.

rows.fak_doc: none — in-kernel forward serves text-only architectures (SmolLM2, Qwen2.5/3.8, Inkling-2, GLM-5.2)
rows.comparison_note: OUT OF SCOPE for a text-tool-loop reuse kernel. fak's in-kernel model executes text-only forward passes (up to 26B Inkling-2-Mini and 27B Qwen3.8 on 1-2 GPUs); there is NO vision encoder, no image-token patch path, and no multimodal RadixAttention. Larger or VLM workloads ride fronted SGLang/vLLM endpoints. Verdict stays no-claim.

rows.fak_doc: README.md (128k all-resident NVFP4 KV on 16 GB RTX 5080); docs/benchmarks/published/rtx5080-inkling2-v060/RESULTS.md (32K auto-FP8 KV)
rows.comparison_note: HW-WITNESSED on 16 GB RTX 5080: fak serves 131,072 (128K) all-resident context with opt-in NVFP4 KV (0 GiB CPU spill, 1,190 tok/s prefill, 16.9 tok/s decode, exact 128k needle retrieval, rev eb68a8cf8a) and 32K auto-FP8 KV by default (rtx5080-inkling2-v060). Trails datacenter multi-GPU SGLang/vLLM 1,000,000-token context deployments (apples_to_apples=false: single 16 GB consumer GPU all-resident vs datacenter multi-GPU / server deployment).

OUT OF SCOPE for the reuse/adjudication kernel. fak has no LoRA adapter loading, no multi-adapter batching, no hot-swap path. Its multi-model story is the polymodel residency Pool (host many full models, share prefill, decode one) — a DIFFERENT primitive (full models, not low-rank adapters) and itself off-mainline/policy-only (CLAIMS polymodel rows, FAK_POLYMODEL default off). No fak LoRA number; verdict no-claim.

rows.fak_doc: none — no pooling/embedding endpoint in CLAIMS
rows.comparison_note: OUT OF SCOPE for a generative-tool-loop reuse kernel. fak serves only causal-LM next-token decode; there is no pooling head, no embeddings endpoint, no cross-encoder reranker path. fak's OpenAI-compatible surface is /v1/chat/completions (CLAIMS Gateway), not /v1/embeddings. No fak number; verdict no-claim.

rows.axis: Hardware backend breadth (NVIDIA, AMD, Intel, TPU, AWS, Apple, CPU)
rows.unit: distinct compute backends shipped (CPU + NVIDIA CUDA + AMD Vulkan + Apple Metal), all single-device
rows.comparison_note: REAL but narrower than SOTA breadth. fak ships four numerically-verified single-device backends: pure-Go CPU (x86 AVX2/AVX-512 + arm64), NVIDIA CUDA (sm_80..sm_120, reaching decode parity & W4A4 prefill lead on 26B Inkling-2-Mini on RTX 5080), AMD Vulkan (RX 7600, Q8/Q4_K/GDN wired; full Qwen3.8 receipt awaiting remeasure), and Apple Metal (internal/metalgemm; retired Splash Inkling-2 port retracted, full M3 Pro resident receipts pending). Still trails vLLM (TPU/Gaudi/Trainium/Ascend/Spyre) and llama.cpp (HIP/SYCL/CANN/OpenCL) on accelerator breadth and non-CUDA GPU maturity.

rows.axis: Capability/quality of the served model (SWE-bench Verified, GPQA, AIME, LiveCodeBench)
rows.competitor: Gemini 3.x (SWE-bench/GPQA); Claude Opus 4.5 + agent scaffold; GPT-5.x (AIME)
rows.fak_doc: industry_scorecard.data.json swebench-resolve-rate row (no-claim/stub); SOTA-COMPARISON.md; CLAIMS: fak is a serving kernel, resolve rate set by the served model
rows.comparison_note: OUT OF SCOPE by construction. fak is a serving KERNEL, not a model: SWE-bench Verified / GPQA / AIME / LiveCodeBench are set entirely by whatever model it serves, so fak claims NO resolve rate of its own. The frontier bars cited (SWE-bench Verified ~79-80.6%, GPQA Diamond ~93-94%, AIME up to 100%) are model-served-by-engine results. fak's claim is orthogonal: ~20-24x prefill-work reduction ON TOP of any model at the same quality, lower infra cost. Carried so the scorecard never quietly omits the headline a frontier-model comparison leads with. Honest no-claim.
